unit: Unit 1: Database System Concepts, ER Model & Relational Design

questions.stem: The Database Administrator (DBA) is primarily responsible for designing the database schema, granting user permissions, managing security, and monitoring database performance.
questions.rationale: True. The DBA has central control over the system, managing security authorizations, physical storage, schema design, and operational backups. (Key Takeaway: The DBA controls database access, schema definition, and maintenance.)

questions.stem: Which geometric shape represents an Entity Set in standard Peter Chen ER notation?

options.text: Ellipse — represents an active relational table

questions.rationale: In Chen ER notation, Rectangles represent Entity Sets, Diamonds represent Relationship Sets, and Ellipses represent Attributes. (Key Takeaway: In ER diagrams, rectangles represent entity sets.)

questions.module_title: Advanced ER and Extended ER (EER) Concepts
questions.stem: In an ER diagram, the Partial Key (Discriminator) of a weak entity set is indicated by a solid underline.
questions.rationale: False — swapped_term. A solid underline indicates a Primary Key of a strong entity set. A partial key (discriminator) of a weak entity set is indicated by a dashed (dotted) underline. (Key Takeaway: Partial keys are marked with dashed underlines; primary keys with solid underlines.)

questions.stem: What is the primary role of a Foreign Key in a relational database?

options.text: An auto-incrementing integer used solely to number rows sequentially
An attribute in one table that references the primary key of another table to maintain referential integrity
A special security password required to connect to international servers

questions.rationale: A Foreign Key is an attribute or set of attributes in a referencing table that matches the primary key of a referenced table, enforcing referential integrity across relations. (Key Takeaway: Foreign keys link tables and enforce referential integrity.)

questions.stem: During ER-to-relational schema mapping, does a Multivalued Attribute (such as multiple skills for an employee) map into a brand new, separate table?
questions.rationale: Yes. Relational 1NF forbids non-atomic or multi-valued fields in a single row. Therefore, every multivalued attribute maps into a separate table containing the attribute and the parent primary key as a foreign key. (Key Takeaway: Multivalued attributes always map to a separate table to satisfy 1NF.)

questions.stem: Which SQL command is used to add a new column to an existing table without erasing or dropping the existing table?

options.text: CREATE TABLE — it recreates the table structure from scratch
ALTER TABLE ... ADD — it adds new column definitions while preserving existing rows
UPDATE TABLE — it writes new schema metadata into temporary memory buffers

questions.rationale: ALTER TABLE is a DDL command that modifies the schema definition of an existing table (e.g., adding or dropping columns) without data loss. (Key Takeaway: ALTER TABLE modifies existing table schemas without deleting stored data.)
